spotVsFutures.q: What is the difference between spot and futures?
spotVsFutures.a: Spot means you actually buy and hold the asset — sell higher to profit, and the most you can lose is what you paid. Futures is margin trading: you never hold the underlying, you can go long or short, leverage amplifies your exposure, and you can be liquidated. Gold and oil here are futures-only instruments (TradFi perpetuals) with no spot to buy, while tokenized US equities are spot.

leverage.a: Leverage lets one unit of capital control several times that size. Open 10x on 100 USDT and you hold a 1,000 USDT position — every 1% move in price is 10% on your capital. Leverage magnifies losses exactly as much as gains, and the higher the multiple the closer liquidation gets. Futures here use tiered leverage (each tier caps position size), and spot buys also offer low-multiple borrowed leverage charged by the day.

crossVsIsolated.q: What is the difference between cross and isolated margin?
crossVsIsolated.a: The difference is what pays for the loss. Isolated: each position stakes only its own margin, so the worst case is losing that one slice and the rest of your funds are untouched. Cross: the whole available balance backs every position, so one losing position eats into the entire account — it survives bigger swings, but a liquidation costs far more. Start with isolated, where the maximum loss is obvious.

markPrice.q: What is the mark price, and why is liquidation based on it?
markPrice.a: The mark price is the fair price an exchange derives from the composite spot index. It is smoother than the last traded price and is what unrealized PnL and liquidation triggers are calculated from. The point is to stop someone pushing the traded price through a thin book with one large order and liquidating others on purpose (a wick). Your position PnL tracks the mark price, not the latest candle price.

liqPrice.q: What is the liquidation price and how is it worked out?
liqPrice.a: When the mark price reaches your liquidation price, the system force-closes the position. Intuitively, the liquidation price is where your margin is nearly used up, minus one more cushion for the maintenance margin rate (MMR). The higher the leverage and the thinner the margin, the closer liquidation sits to your entry. The order panel estimates it live; once you hold a position, switch on position lines in the chart toolbar and entry, TP/SL and liquidation are drawn straight onto the chart.

mmr.q: What is the maintenance margin rate (MMR)?
mmr.a: The minimum margin ratio a position needs to avoid liquidation. It is tiered by notional value: the larger the position, the higher the tier and the higher the MMR — big positions are harder to unwind, so they are required to carry a thicker cushion. Liquidation triggers when margin + unrealized PnL < position value × MMR.

fundingRate.q: What is the funding rate, and why does holding a position cost money?
fundingRate.a: Perpetual futures never settle, so funding keeps the contract price tethered to spot: when the rate is positive longs pay shorts, when it is negative the reverse. Here it is charged three times a day (aligned with Binance settlement times) on notional value, using the live Binance rate for the current period and falling back to a fixed +0.01% only when the feed fails. This is the main cost of sitting in a position for a long time — the position card shows the estimate for each period.

tpSl.q: How do take profit and stop loss work?
tpSl.a: Every futures position can carry several TP/SL levels, each with its own price and size. When the mark price reaches one it executes at market and you get a notification. Getting stopped out is nothing to be ashamed of — the campaign even awards points for it under "Stop-loss hero". Decide your exit before you enter: liquidation is losing by default, a stop loss is losing on your own terms.

doubleLiq.q: What does a long-short double liquidation mean in the liquidation feed?
doubleLiq.a: The liquidation feed shows force-closed orders from across the site, including the Binance liquidation stream. In violent moves one side goes first — a sharp drop takes out the longs — and then the snap-back takes out everyone who chased the short. That is a long-short double liquidation, and it is often read as a sign of extreme sentiment and a possible short-term reversal.

bankrupt.q: What happens if I go bankrupt?
bankrupt.a: When your trading net worth (cash + position value − borrowed principal and interest) falls below zero, the system marks you bankrupt: all wallets and positions are cleared and your starting capital is restored on the next trading day so you can begin again. Note that an automatic bankruptcy recovery still counts against your weekly resets — during the campaign, going bankrupt after you have already reset this week is charged as a paid reset and costs 30 campaign points.

prediction.q: How does the prediction market work?
prediction.a: You bet on future events with the game wallet: the price is the probability the market implies, so buy the side you believe in and hold to settlement, which pays 1 if you were right and 0 if you were not. You can also sell early to lock in the result. During the campaign, single bets of 100 or more held to a winning settlement also earn campaign points, subject to tiered caps — it is not farmable.

dailyVote.q: What is the daily long-short vote?
dailyVote.a: Every day you vote on whether BTC and gold go up or down tomorrow. The target is tomorrow's UTC daily candle and voting closes tonight, so there is no hindsight; it settles after 08:00 the next morning on the daily close. A pool of 100 points a day is split among everyone who was right: the crowded side gets less per head and a correct contrarian call gets more, capped at 6 points per person per day.

wallets.q: Are the game wallet and the trading wallet the same thing?
wallets.a: No. The main wallet is for trading (spot, futures, stocks), while the game wallet funds Mines, Video Poker, Blackjack and the prediction market. They are accounted for separately and there is an entry to transfer between them. Bankruptcy is judged on trading net worth alone — the game wallet cannot save you, and it is wiped along with everything else.

coupon.a: Discount coupons from the daily buff draw are ticked on when you place a spot market buy, cutting the fill amount by the coupon rate. The "Saved" figure on the leaderboard is the total you have discounted this way. The rarer the coupon the steeper the discount, so keep the legendary ones for large orders.

campaign.q: What are campaign points and the LDC prize pool?
campaign.a: During the five-dimension trading contest you earn points from trading (ROI targets and net PnL), the daily check-in, the long-short vote, the prediction market, comments and more; the campaign page lists every task along with your live breakdown. Liquidations and similar events deduct points. When the campaign ends, the LDC prize pool is split by final point weight — authorize your LinuxDo account on the campaign page to claim your share. Resetting your account does not clear points you have already earned.

resetAccount.q: What are the rules for resetting an account?
resetAccount.a: A reset clears all positions, orders, game records and asset history, and returns your balance to the starting capital; comments, mute status and campaign points are unaffected. During the campaign the first reset in each calendar week is free and every reset after that costs 30 campaign points; once the campaign ends it is one reset per week, refreshed on Monday. An automatic bankruptcy recovery counts toward the same quota.
